column1: # #373 round 3 — the single work queue, in priority order.
# One queue, four GPUs: 2 on the rented box, 2 on elisa. q_run.sh reads this
# file top to bottom and slides the first ready job onto the first free slot.
# Columns: id  type  cell  stop  enc  depends_on
#   type bb    train the backbone to <stop> steps
#   type head  train one quantile head off that stop's checkpoint
#   type eval  the 97-config GIFT-Eval of that head (CPU, elisa)
# Order: B8 first (the one cell with no bb100k), then the eight extends
# biggest bb100k winner first. A4 extends the student head only — the extend
# rule gave one head down for it. B1 extends by the card's call. Its bb40k
# pair IS its own — round 1 wrote it as score_G6_B1_k3_bb40k_*, off checkpoint
# md5 23ba3d9d..., the file round 2 resumed, at the same 15,000-step head —
# The five cells the rule stopped at 100k are absent on purpose:
# B8's bb40k pair. Every other cell carries a 40k number; B8 is the only
# hole in that column, and its backbone saves 40k on the way to 100k, so the
# pair costs one 15,000-step head each and two CPU evals. Last in the queue:
# it must never delay a stop the plan asked for. Head steps follow the other
# thirteen cells' bb40k heads, 15,000, or the column is not comparable.
# 2026-08-12 21:10 — the dependency on bb_B8_100k is released. B8's backbone
# writes its 40k checkpoint on the way to 100k and already has, so these two
# heads read a file that exists. They stay LAST in the file, so they take a
# slot only after every stop the plan asked for has one, and the only slots
# they can take are the two head-only ones, which no backbone may use. Those
# two sat idle for four hours behind a dependency that was already satisfied.
# 2026-08-13 13:02 — A4's teacher head at bb200k. The extend rule read
# +0.0019 from bb40k to bb100k on this head and returned `stop`, but the
# rule compares raw numbers with no band, and +0.0019 is far inside the
# ±0.0384 head-seed band. That is B1's situation, which the card extended
# by hand. A4 is the study's strongest cell and its 200k backbone already
# exists, so the head costs one elisa card and the eval costs cores. No
# rented hardware is involved. The head is already running outside the
# queue (state pre-set to `running`); this row exists so the eval behind
# it dispatches and the publisher carries both.
